task: t43 (repair of t38's V1: an interjection request without content was silently invisible)
defect: lib/state.js enqueueInterjection spread the caller object and never validated content; the mailbox shape check on read REQUIRES a non-empty string content, so a request without content returned status:'pending' while readPendingInterjections could not see it and decideInterjection reported the misleading 'interjection "<id>" does not exist'. Captain silence could therefore never expire it.
decision: OPTION (b) NORMALIZATION, not a loud rejection: content is derived in a FIXED priority order summary -> reason -> location; id/from/ts remain REQUIRED and are rejected loudly, naming the field, because no fallback can invent an identity or a clock.
whyNormalizationChosen: A rejection would also close the hole, but it pushes the burden onto every caller and the shipped callers are LLM-driven; normalization keeps a well-formed, decidable record for the common malformed shape while the loud rejection still covers the fields that cannot be defaulted. The decision is PINNED by tests so it cannot drift silently.

changes.enqueueInterjection: validates id/from/ts (throws naming the missing field) and normalizes content (summary->reason->location); the doc block states the contract and the priority.
changes.readRawInterjectionRecords: new internal lenient reader (JSON parse, NO shape check) so a present-but-malformed record is distinguishable from an absent one.
changes.decideInterjection: now throws a DISTINCT error when the id is present on disk but fails the shape check ('exists but is MALFORMED ...'), instead of the misleading 'does not exist'.
